div.head: Shiji I: Basic Annals
div.p: Basic Annals of Qin: In the autumn of the fifty-sixth year, King Zhaoxiang died, and his son King Xiaowen was set up. He honoured the Bazi consort Tang as Queen Dowager Tang and buried her together with the late king. The King of Han, in hempen mourning dress, came in to condole and sacrifice, and the Lords all sent their generals and ministers to come and condole and sacrifice, and to attend to the funeral.

div.head: Shiji II: Tables
div.p: Chu: The Pillar of the State Jing Bo died.
Yan: Attacked Zhao; Zhao defeated our army and killed Li Fu.

div.head: Shiji III: Hereditary Houses
div.p: Hereditary House of Duke Shao of Yan: In the fourth year of the present king, Xi, King Zhao of Qin died. The King of Yan ordered the Chancellor Li Fu to conclude friendly relations with Zhao, and with five hundred jin of gold he feasted the King of Zhao. He returned and reported to the King of Yan: "Of the King of Zhao's men, those in their prime all died at Changping, and their orphans are not yet grown; he can be attacked." The king summoned Lord Changguo, Yue Jian, and asked him. He replied: "Zhao is a state at war on four sides; its people are practised in arms. It cannot be attacked." The king said: "I shall attack with five against one." He replied: "It cannot be done." The King of Yan was angry, and the assembled ministers all held that it could be done. In the end he raised two armies, two thousand chariots: Li Fu led one and attacked Hao, and Qing Qin attacked Dai. Alone the Grand Master Jiang Qu said to the King of Yan: "To open the Passes to another and bind oneself to him in friendship, to feast another's king with five hundred jin of gold, and then, when the envoy has reported back, to turn and attack him — that is ill-omened, and the troops will have no success." The King of Yan did not listen, and himself led a detached army behind them. Jiang Qu took hold of the King of Yan's seal-ribbon to stop him, saying: "Your Majesty must on no account go yourself; if you go there will be no success." The king kicked him away with his foot. Jiang Qu wept and said: "Your servant does this not for himself but for Your Majesty!" The Yan army reached Songzi. Zhao sent Lian Po in command; he struck and defeated Li Fu at Hao. Yue Cheng defeated Qing Qin at Dai. Yue Jian fled to Zhao. Lian Po pursued them more than five hundred li and besieged their capital. The men of Yan sued for peace; the men of Zhao would not allow it, and insisted that Jiang Qu be made to handle the peace. Yan made Jiang Qu Chancellor to handle the peace. Zhao heeded Jiang Qu and raised the siege of Yan.
Hereditary House of Chu: In the twelfth year, King Zhao of Qin died, and the King of Chu sent Lord Chunshen to condole and sacrifice in Qin.

Hereditary House of Zhao: In the fifteenth year, the Chancellor of State Lian Po was enfeoffed with Weiwen as Lord Xinping. The King of Yan ordered the Chancellor Li Fu to conclude friendly relations, and with five hundred jin of gold he feasted the King of Zhao; he went back and reported to the King of Yan: "Of the men of Zhao, those in their prime all died at Changping, and their orphans are not yet grown; Zhao can be attacked." The king summoned Lord Changguo, Yue Jian, and asked him. He replied: "Zhao is a state at war on four sides; its people are practised in arms. To attack it cannot be done." The king said: "If I attack the few with the many, two against one, will it do?" He replied: "It will not." The king said: "Then if I attack with five against one, will it do?" He replied: "It will not." The King of Yan was greatly angered. The assembled ministers all held that it could be done. Yan in the end raised two armies, two thousand chariots: Li Fu led one and attacked Hao, and Qing Qin led one and attacked Dai. Lian Po was Zhao's general; he defeated and killed Li Fu and captured Qing Qin and Yue Jian.
Hereditary House of Wei: In the twenty-sixth year, King Zhao of Qin died.
Hereditary House of Han: In the twenty-second year, King Zhao of Qin died.
